'''Radio Free Decipher''' ('''RFD''') was Decipher's weekly RealAudio show, 4 December 1998 – 30 April 2004, about 196 episodes. It predated the word podcast. Topics included SWCCG, Young Jedi, Jedi Knights, Star Trek CCG, Austin Powers, spoilers, DecipherCon, and staff interviews.<ref name="lotrpc-rfd">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Radio_Free_Decipher Radio Free Decipher], LOTR-TCG Player's Council wiki (episode index: dates, hosts, lengths, missing files).</ref>

== History ==

RFD was streamed from Decipher's website, decipher.com, and kept in an online archive of past broadcasts.<ref name="rfd-archive">[http://web.archive.org/web/20080509090404/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index.html RFD archive], Decipher (decipher.com). Preserved copy: [http://web.archive.org/web/20080509090404/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher described the show as "the authentic voice" of its Young Jedi, Austin Powers, Star Trek and Star Wars CCGs "and the people who make them". It also aired special broadcasts from the road and from DecipherCon.<ref name="rfd-facts">[http://web.archive.org/web/20080511223849/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/factsandtips/index.html RFD facts and tips], Decipher (decipher.com). Preserved copy: [http://web.archive.org/web/20080511223849/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/factsandtips/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

[[Carol Wisely]] (VP of Marketing) hosted originally. After episode 30, [[Kyle Heuer]] and [[Evan Lorentz]] took over regular hosting.<ref name="lotrpc-rfd" /> Early SWCCG-heavy episodes also feature [[Kendrick Summers]], [[Jerry Darcy]], [[Chuck Kallenbach]], [[Tom Lischke]], [[Kevin Reitzel]], [[Sandy Wible]], [[Bill Martinson]], [[Justin Pakes]], [[Joe Alread]], [[Marcus Certa]], and squadron call-ins ([[Alex Alcalde]], [[Carl "Mike" Hardy]], [[Guy Kargl]]).

From late 2001 the show was dominated by The Lord of the Rings TCG, which Decipher released in November 2001, and by Star Trek CCG Second Edition. The last Star Wars-focused broadcasts deal with the end of the license and the handover of the game to the [[Players Committee]].

=== Special Broadcast, 28 December 2001 ===

On 28 December 2001 Decipher released a Star Wars special broadcast in which CEO [[Warren Holland]] was interviewed by Kyle Heuer.<ref name="yt-ZpXfkPyurfE">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council (18 February 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="ann122801">[http://web.archive.org/web/20080215111820/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/announcement122801.html Star Wars CCG announcement, 28 December 2001], Decipher (decipher.com). Preserved copy: [http://web.archive.org/web/20080215111820/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/announcement122801.html Internet Archive].</ref> Holland announced that Lucasfilm would not renew Decipher's Star Wars CCG license past the end of 2001. The manufacturing and sell-off period ran through 30 April 2002.<ref name="yt-ZpXfkPyurfE" /> He said Decipher had offered Lucasfilm more than it had offered for any license in its history. The offer exceeded the budget of the original ''Star Wars'' film and was six times what Decipher had paid for ''Episode I''.<ref name="yt-ZpXfkPyurfE" />

Holland described a final product that Lucasfilm turned down. Decipher had pitched logo cards for each of the four films, with game text on a web page "totally administered by a players committee". The committee could then issue the equivalent of a new virtual expansion every four to six months.<ref name="yt-ZpXfkPyurfE" /> In its place he announced "a non-profit players group called the Players Committee for Star Wars CCGs", a small body of volunteer players and playtesters. At the end of April 2002 Decipher would turn over rules support, FAQs, tournament prize support, the web pages and World Championship duties to the committee. It would donate cards for those duties, and the committee could select existing cards and post replacement text for them as tournament-legal virtual cards.<ref name="yt-ZpXfkPyurfE" /> Holland also said Decipher had about 300 unreleased cards in development, about 100 of them virtual cards. Subject to Lucasfilm approval, Decipher hoped to release them free on the web as a PDF.<ref name="yt-ZpXfkPyurfE" />

The following regular broadcasts carried the Players Committee news: Broadcast 110 (11 January 2002)<ref name="yt-8aNpe-I-KQk" /> and Broadcast 112 with [[Scott Gaeta]] (25 January 2002).<ref name="yt-docK2vpQWUI" />

=== Successors ===

The last RFD, Broadcast 196 (30 April 2004), featured [[Tim Ellington]] on Decipher's new [[WARS TCG]].<ref name="yt-5K5m0Yywu_Q" /> Successors: [[WARS Radio|Decipher WARS Radio]] (25 June 2004 – 21 January 2005, host [[Mark Tuttle]]) and a short [[Decipher Games Radio]] (March–April 2005).<ref name="lotrpc-rfd" />

== Surviving audio ==

The LOTR-TCG Players Committee ([[Player's Council (YouTube channel)|Player's Council]]) rehosted surviving audio on YouTube and keeps an episode index.<ref name="lotrpc-rfd" /><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLYLMRQ0b_feAbpbNVQwlw3y8XH30ZQS1U RFD YouTube playlist], Player's Council</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLYLMRQ0b_feBmwx60mQf1kO7fv09DfnrE Decipher radio master playlist], Player's Council</ref> Many Wayback files truncate at 1&nbsp;MB (~8:43) because of a contemporary RealAudio streaming bug.<ref name="rfd-facts" /> Evan Lorentz's own files supplied most of the missing audio. A handful of episodes remain missing.<ref name="lotrpc-rfd" /> Copies of the YouTube uploads are kept on the Internet Archive.

== Selected SWCCG episodes ==

* Broadcast 2 (11 December 1998): [[Jerry Darcy]], [[Tom Lischke]] and [[Chuck Kallenbach]] on operatives<ref name="yt-w2Ao759YJlk" />
* Broadcast 7 (29 January 1999): Chuck Kallenbach on the Hidden Base errata<ref name="yt-Y7OxVn3HP_k" />
* Broadcasts 12 and 13 (2 and 9 April 1999): [[Bill Martinson]] and Jerry Darcy on Product Development<ref name="yt-DsqnSbxT25c" />
* Broadcasts 14 and 16 (16 and 30 April 1999): the original designers [[Rollie Tesh]] and [[Tom Braunlich]]<ref name="yt-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw" />
* Broadcast 39 (23 June 2000): Chuck Kallenbach on Enhanced Maul<ref name="yt-D5SfiJExRV0" />
* Broadcast 90 (3 August 2001): [[Justin Pakes]] on SWCCG design<ref name="yt-oDR3IRuAbhI" />
* Broadcast 93 (24 August 2001): [[Brian Kallenbach]] and Will Purdue on playtesting<ref name="yt-OI9-Uc0QPw4" />
* Broadcast 99 (5 October 2001): [[Warren Holland]] on the cancellation of DecipherCon after the September 11 attacks<ref name="yt-wS84wdG4EUI" />
* Special Broadcast (28 December 2001): Warren Holland on the end of the license and the [[Players Committee]]<ref name="yt-ZpXfkPyurfE" />
* Broadcast 110 (11 January 2002): news of the Star Wars Players Committee<ref name="yt-8aNpe-I-KQk" />
* Broadcast 112 (25 January 2002): [[Scott Gaeta]] on the SWCCG Players Committee<ref name="yt-docK2vpQWUI" />
* Broadcast 119 (15 March 2002): Chris and MaryGail Coffee on the SWCCG Open<ref name="yt-8KvLjZofZcY" />
